title: Indian Jazz Musician Pritesh Walia Released on Bond After 14 Days in ICE Detention
excerpt: The Berklee-educated guitarist was detained at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center after returning to Los Angeles on August 2, with no official explanation from immigration authorities.
body:
• Indian-born jazz guitarist Pritesh Walia was released on bond after spending 14 days in ICE detention at the Adelanto Processing Center in California.
  • Walia was detained on August 2 upon returning to Los Angeles, with his phone and personal belongings confiscated; ICE has not issued any official statement on the reason for his arrest.
  • The Berklee College of Music graduate held an O-1B artist visa and has over 57,000 Instagram followers; his detention drew widespread support from the jazz music community.
  • The case adds to a growing pattern of Indian nationals and visa holders being detained by immigration authorities amid heightened ICE enforcement across the United States.

Detained Without Explanation

Pritesh Walia, an Indian-born jazz guitarist with degrees from some of America's most prestigious music schools, was released on bond after 14 days in immigration detention, according to a post on his Instagram account and reporting by Aaj Tak.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2089519244883239232

Walia was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement on the night of August 2 after returning to Los Angeles with a friend. He was subsequently transferred to the Adelanto ICE Processing Center in California's high desert, where his phone and personal belongings were confiscated, cutting him off from contact with the outside world.

"This is Liza. I'm currently managing Pritesh's account on his behalf," read a statement posted to Walia's Instagram account shortly after his detention. "His personal belongings, including his phone, were taken upon detention, and he currently has no access to them."

ICE has not issued any official statement regarding the detention or the grounds for Walia's arrest, as reported by 7Globe.

A Musician's American Journey

Walia was born in New Delhi and began studying Indian classical music at the age of 13 before moving to the United States to pursue higher education in music. He earned an Associate's degree from the Musician's Institute in Los Angeles, a Bachelor's degree from the Berklee College of Music in Boston, and a Master's degree from the New England Conservatory, according to media reports.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=687Wu7QQQWE

He held an O-1B visa — commonly known as an artist visa — reserved for individuals with extraordinary ability or achievement in the arts. The initial validity period for the visa is three years. Neither Walia nor ICE has disclosed the specific immigration issue that led to his detention, though online speculation suggested his visa may have lapsed.

In 2023, Walia faced a serious health crisis, being diagnosed with Persistent Postural Perceptual Dizziness, Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, and chronic vestibular migraines. Friends organized a fundraiser to support his treatment after the conditions prevented him from performing, according to 7Globe.

Release and an Outpouring of Support

After his release on bond, Walia posted an emotional message on Instagram thanking his family, girlfriend, attorney, and the broader jazz music community for their support during his detention.

"On behalf of Pritesh's family, we would like to immensely thank all of his well-wishers and supporters. We are extremely grateful and request you to keep him in your prayers, so that he finds all the strength he needs to fight this most uncalled-for crisis."

— A family member posting on Reddit during Walia's detention

Walia, who has over 57,000 followers on Instagram, described feeling "completely broken" at times during his two weeks in custody, but said the hundreds of messages of support from outside gave him the strength to endure, according to Aaj Tak. He has since stepped away from the public spotlight to rest and spend time with family.

A Pattern of Detentions

Walia's case is the latest in a growing list of Indian nationals and visa holders facing detention by ICE. In recent months, an Indian-origin woman was detained during her green card interview after three decades in the United States, and federal courts have ordered the release of multiple Indian citizens detained without proper hearings in California.

Immigration experts have warned visa holders to exercise heightened caution, with some advising against even domestic travel. ICE surveillance and arrests at airports have increased significantly under the current administration's enforcement posture, according to reporting by 7Globe.

Walia's release on bond does not resolve his immigration case. He still faces legal proceedings, and the uncertainty around his status in the country remains. For now, the musician who crossed oceans to study and perform in America waits to learn whether his American chapter will continue.
nri_angle: An Indian-born musician with elite American music credentials was detained by ICE with no explanation, highlighting the precarious status of Indian visa holders amid heightened immigration enforcement.
author: Diaspora Desk
